sections.h2: What are your choices if you need to sell in White Plains quickly?
sections.html:
Three routes exist: an agent listing, a private sale, or a buyer who pays cash and accepts the house in its present condition. Downtown White Plains also holds the Westchester County government, so the courts, the deed recording office and the city's permit and tax desks are a short drive apart.

Speed here depends mostly on the file. An open permit, a missing certificate or an unpaid installment tends to stall a closing once the attorneys start reviewing, whatever the buyer's financing. What follows covers the documents, the tax calendar and the recording steps that set the pace.

sections.h2: How do White Plains owners and renters compare?
sections.html:
Owners and renters are nearly even in number here, and prices run high. The 2020 count was 59,559 people, and the latest federal estimate, dated July 1, 2025, is 62,871, which is 5.6 percent above the 2020 base.

At $2,269 a month in the middle of the rent range, a tenanted house can attract someone shopping for income, and that buyer will ask to see leases and payment history. Land area is 9.74 square miles, roughly 6,117 people per square mile, so lots are compact.

sections.h2: How did White Plains grow, and which neighborhoods matter to sellers?
sections.html:
A party from Connecticut purchased roughly 4,400 acres here in November 1683. The place took over as Westchester's county seat in 1758, incorporated as a village in 1866 and became a city in 1916. The Battle of White Plains was fought in October 1776 around Chatterton Hill, and a copy of the Declaration of Independence was read from the courthouse steps that July.

Postwar downtown became a department store district, and a late 1960s urban renewal plan reshaped the core around the county courthouse, the Galleria mall and office towers. City Center later added two 35-story residential towers. Offices, hospitals and courts keep the weekday population far above the resident count, at about 250,000 by the city government's estimate.

Dozens of named neighborhoods exist, and buyers search by them. A few of the better known:

  • Gedney and Fisher Hill.
  • The Highlands, with Lower and Upper sections.
  • Rosedale, which has its own small subsections such as Rosedale Gardens and Rosedale Estates.
  • Battle Hill, Soundview, Eastview, Carhart and Haviland Manor.
  • North White Plains and the North Street area.

ZIP code 10605, in the southern part of the city, is mostly single-family housing.

sections.h2: Why do trains and schools matter when pricing a White Plains house?
sections.html:
Commuting access is the feature buyers mention first. Metro-North's Harlem Line stops twice in the city, downtown at Main Street and the Bronx River and again in North White Plains, and an express run to Midtown takes about 31 minutes.

  • Rail: both city stations are on the Harlem Line.
  • Roads: the Cross-Westchester Expressway (I-287) and the Bronx River Parkway.
  • Buses: Bee-Line routes meet at the Trans-Center next to the downtown station.
  • Air: Westchester County Airport sits in Harrison, about seven miles northeast.

The city's public school system covers elementary through high school, and since 1988 it has run a parents' choice program for elementary placement. Families may rank schools on factors other than distance, so an address does not lock in one elementary school.

sections.h2: How does White Plains weather affect an older house?
sections.html:
Cold wet winters and hot summers both load the building. Readings at Westchester County Airport put the January mean at 29.8 degrees and July at 74.0, with about 47.75 inches of precipitation and 27.7 inches of snow across a normal year. Records since 1948 range from minus 10 to 102 degrees.

A buyer's inspector will therefore look first at the roof, gutters, basement walls and heating system. If you know of a past leak or boiler repair, pull the paperwork together before listing.

sections.h2: What does the White Plains Building Department want to see on a certificate of occupancy?
sections.html:
Under the city's rule, no building may be occupied, and no occupancy class changed, before the Commissioner of Building issues a Certificate of Occupancy. The department works from 70 Church Street, phone 914-422-1269.

Every permitted job must be completed and inspected by the Building Department, the Fire Department and any other agency involved. For a missing certificate, the FAQ points owners to a Building Short Form with the Updated and Substitute CO type, plus the fee, after which a code enforcement officer inspects. A temporary certificate can issue once life safety and public health items are cleared.

  • A Certificate of Compliance covers decks, additions and alterations that leave the building's use unchanged.
  • The department suggests obtaining one for any work done under a building permit.
  • Ask for the current fee before applying, since fees are set by building type.

sections.h2: What are the White Plains tax due dates, and what about water bills at closing?
sections.html:
Three payments fall due each year, and the last day of the due month is the cutoff. After that, interest runs at 1 percent per month, and the Finance Department states that it has no power to waive it.

  • July 1: first half of the city and school levy, late from August 1.
  • January 1: second half of the city and school levy, late from February 1.
  • April 1: the county levy, late from May 1.

Bills go out in mid-December, late March and June. Under Real Property Tax Law Section 922 a bill that fails to arrive changes nothing, so call the tax office if yours is missing. Make checks payable to the Commissioner of Finance, 255 Main Street, Room 102.

Water adds a seller's task. A final reading costs $75 and is requested at 914-422-1211, and unpaid water charges come back onto the property as a tax lien on the following July 1. Ownership on the tax roll changes only after the Assessor's Office gets a certified copy of the recorded deed.

sections.h2: How do you challenge a White Plains assessment?
sections.html:
The Assessor's Office runs on a fixed yearly calendar, and the complaint window is short. December 1 is the taxable status date, the tentative roll is dated January 1, complaints are taken January 1 to 21, and the final roll lands on March 1. Exemptions are handled from April 1 through December 1.

The 2026 final roll is posted on the city's website. Since one assessed value drives both the city and school bills, a seller who finds it too high should collect recent nearby sales before January. The office is at 255 Main Street, phone 914-422-1223.

sections.h2: What does recording a White Plains deed involve?
sections.html:
The state charges the seller a base transfer tax per $500 of price, rounded up to the next $500, and the buyer owes an added 1 percent when a residence sells for $1 million or more. Form TP-584 travels with the deed to the county clerk, and payment is due within 15 days of delivery.

The Westchester County Clerk's Land Records Division takes a deed only with four documents generated in its PREP system: a recording cover sheet, the TP-584, the RP-5217 transfer report and a payment cover sheet. Originals come back after scanning, and anyone needing a certified copy fast should order it with the submission.

faqs.q: Who is billed for White Plains tax after a sale?
faqs.a: The owner of record, until the Assessor's Office is sent a certified copy of the recorded deed. Send it promptly, and file the city's Tax Account Change Form if the bill needs a new mailing address.

faqs.q: What would state transfer tax come to on a $620,800 White Plains sale?
faqs.a: About $2,484. The price rounds up to $621,000, or 1,242 units of $500 at $2 apiece, and the seller pays unless the contract assigns it to the buyer.

faqs.q: What if no White Plains tax bill arrives?
faqs.a: The tax and any interest are still owed. Call the Finance Department at 914-422-1248 to verify the address and request a duplicate.

faqs.q: When is the White Plains complaint window?
faqs.a: From January 1 to January 21 each year. The next one opens January 1, 2027, against the tentative roll.

faqs.q: Is a missing Certificate of Occupancy a problem for a White Plains sale?
faqs.a: It is best to resolve it first, since the city bars occupancy without one and a buyer's attorney is likely to ask. The route is a Building Short Form for an Updated and Substitute CO, then an inspection.
